title: The Smoothie Bar
strapline: Chop it, drop it, whizz it, pour it — and taste the colour you just invented.
intent: Making real smoothies gives children a fast, vivid experience of change — whole fruit becomes a thick, coloured drink in seconds, and they made it happen.
Chopping soft fruit with a table knife builds hand strength and safe, confident tool use with a genuine job to do.
Choosing what goes in, predicting the colour and tasting the result invites real decision-making, prediction and describing.
A smoothie bar is naturally inclusive — every child can pour, press and drink, and there is no way to fail at inventing a flavour.
Trying fruit they helped prepare tempts children to taste more widely, including fruits new to them, because it is theirs.
Counting scoops, sharing out cups and pouring fairly weave number and turn-taking through the whole activity.
implementation: Set out washed soft fruit, table knives and chopping boards, and let children do the real cutting with close, calm supervision.
Let children choose the combinations and predict aloud: 'what colour do you think blueberries and banana will make?'
Use a blender as the shared 'big reveal', naming the change — 'watch, it was lumpy, now it's smooth and purple!'
Make it a bar with a menu, cups, straws and a price board so the pouring and serving has a sociable shape.
Count scoops and share cups fairly — 'four friends waiting, how many cups?' — and pour to a line so it's even.
Name and celebrate fruit from many kitchens, and taste every invention together at the end.
key_questions: What colour do you think blueberries and banana will make?
Watch — it was lumpy, now it's smooth and purple! What happened?
Four friends waiting — how many cups do we need?
How many scoops shall we put in?
What shall we call the flavour you invented?
